issues.description: The problem specification (UML and description) declares calculateRemainingOrderNumber() should return an int (the number of remaining orders). The reference solution implements calculateRemainingOrderNumber() as a void method that prints order lines instead of returning an integer. This is a concrete method return-type mismatch that will confuse students about the required API and return behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the implementation and the specification consistent. Either change the solution to implement public int calculateRemainingOrderNumber() that returns the number of remaining orders (e.g., return orders.length) and avoid printing, or update the problem statement and UML to declare a void method that prints order information. Preferably follow the UML/spec and have the method return an int.

issues.description: Within the problem statement itself there is an inconsistency: the text and UML state calculateRemainingOrderNumber() should return an int (the remaining order count), but the example immediately below shows printed lines ("Order number: ..."), which suggests a void printing behavior. This internal contradiction can confuse students about whether the method should return a value or perform printing.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the intended behavior in the problem statement: either (A) require calculateRemainingOrderNumber() to return an int and remove the printing example, or (B) change the UML/signature to void and state that the method should print the order numbers. Ensure the example, UML, and descriptive text all match the same choice.
